title: Tesla unveils Cyberfied new Roadster that can kickflip
summary:
Tesla has unveiled a new version of its next-generation Roadster. As expected, it received Tesla’s latest design “cyberfication” and cold-gas thrusters to allow it to jump and flip through the air.

The livestream featured impressive stunts but offered few details. Tesla released more information on X after the event, but there’s still no price and no production date.

title: Company that put gas engines in Teslas goes bankrupt owing $37 million
summary:
Obrist, the Austrian engineering firm famous for ripping battery cells out of a Tesla Model 3 and bolting a gas engine into the frunk, is bankrupt. Three companies in the Obrist Group are insolvent with combined debts of about €31.8 million, or roughly $37 million.

The company spent over a decade pitching its “HyperHybrid” range extender as the smarter alternative to battery-electric cars. It never got a single production vehicle out of it.

title: Rivian limits point-to-point driving to invite-only testers under NDA
summary:
Rivian’s point-to-point driving feature will first reach owners through an invitation-only “Autonomy Early Access Program,” and the owners it picks will have to sign a non-disclosure agreement to get in.

The program, laid out on a new Rivian support page, covers US R1 Gen 2 and R2 owners who pay for Autonomy+. Rivian says point-to-point launches to that group in late 2026 and won’t expand broadly until 2027.

title: Tesla remote operators keep crashing its ‘Robotaxis,’ data shows
summary:

That brings it to five in the data now. And every remote takeover that has shown up in a Tesla crash report has ended in a collision.
